column2: On EURUSD, 1 pip = 0.0001. The difference is 1.1035 − 1.1000 = 0.0035, so 0.0035 ÷ 0.0001 = 35 pips.
Roughly how much is one pip worth on EURUSD for a 0.10-lot position?
0.10 lots means 10,000 units. Pip value = 0.0001 × 10,000 = 1 USD. For 1 lot it would be 10 USD, and for 0.01 lots, 0.10 USD.
The cost (sometimes a small gain) of holding a position overnight, based on the interest rates of the two currencies
The difference between the buy price and the sell price
The fee you pay when you open your account
The order that automatically closes your position at a loss

Swap applies to positions held overnight and depends on the interest rates of the two currencies. At most brokers it is charged triple on Wednesdays, to cover the weekend. It matters for swing trading.
You have an account with 1:30 leverage and open a position worth €10,000. How much margin does your broker lock up?
Required margin = position value ÷ leverage = 10,000 ÷ 30 ≈ €333.33. Careful: profit and loss are calculated on the full position value, not on the margin.
What is the maximum leverage for a retail client on EURUSD at an EU-regulated broker?
ESMA caps leverage for EU retail clients at 1:30 on pairs made up only of USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD and CHF. In the EU you also get negative balance protection.
You want to buy EURUSD only if the price drops to a better level, below the current price. Which order do you use?
Limit orders wait for a better price: buy limit below the current price, sell limit above it. Stop orders wait for confirmation: buy stop above the current price.
You're in a buy position and the price is approaching your stop loss. What does the lesson say?
You never move the stop loss further away; you may only move it to reduce risk, if your plan says so
You move the stop loss lower to give the market more room
You remove the stop loss, because price usually comes back
You add another position to get a better average price
The stop loss goes where your idea is proven wrong (for a buy, below the last relevant low) and is never moved further away. Without an SL, a single news release can wipe out months of work.
You risk 25 pips to make 50 (R:R 1:2). What minimum win rate do you need to break even, before costs?
Break-even rate = 1 ÷ (1 + 2) = 33.3%. With R:R 1:1 you would need more than 50%. This is a calculation, not a promise of profit.
You have a €1,500 account and follow the 1% rule. What is the most you can lose if your stop loss is hit?
€1 per pip, whatever the stop loss
1% of €1,500 = €15. It looks small, and that's exactly the point: you can be wrong many times without being knocked out of the game. When you're starting out, even 0.5% is a very good choice.
€2,000 account, 1% risk, 40-pip stop loss on EURUSD at a rate of 1.10 (1 pip on 1 lot ≈ €9.09). Which lot size do you choose?
Amount at risk = €20. Lot = 20 ÷ (40 × 9.09) ≈ 0.055, which rounded down gives 0.05 lots (risk ≈ €18.18). With 0.06 lots you would risk ≈ €21.82, above 1%. Always round down.
Your account drops by 50%. What gain do you need, on what's left, to get back to where you started?
From €1,000 you lose 50% and are left with €500. To get back to €1,000 you need +€500, which is +100% of what you have left. That's why big losses are so hard to recover.
You've lost two trades in a row and feel the urge to "win it back" right away with a bigger lot. What do you do?
Close the platform until the next day: that urge is revenge trading
Double the lot to recover faster
Jump on the first signal without checking your plan
Switch strategies, because it obviously doesn't work
Revenge trading usually leads to bigger lots and bigger losses. The antidote from the lesson: after 2 losses in a row, close the platform until the next day.
What is the recommended first step before trading with real money?
At least 6 to 8 weeks on a demo account, with the same risk, the same plan and a complete journal
A large deposit, so you have room for losses
Copying the signals of a trader with good results
As much leverage as possible, to grow the account quickly
Demo first: at least 6 to 8 weeks and 30 to 50 trades, treated like real money. Go live only if you've been disciplined, with small amounts and 0.01 lots.
